mechanisms.statement: A cut-off sample writes no answer marker, so it abstains from the plurality vote instead of voting wrong. A vote's gain over one sample therefore scales with the cap-hit share times the precision of finished answers: Think-SFT (29-46 % capped, 80-88 % precise) votes near pass@4, while RL and the 1.5x edit (5-15 % capped) gain less. A longer cap turns abstentions into mostly wrong late answers, so a vote gains far less from it than one sample does.

Adding RL-delta weight moves the stopping point earlier: cap hits fall with dose (Think-SFT 94.5 to 33, base 77 to 5), and the cut work becomes finished answers at the host's long-problem precision.

mechanisms.statement: The stop decision responds to the root of the summed squared singular values an edit adds per matrix, whatever its rank: one RL direction at 1x cut cap hits as eight at 0.5x did (51 vs 50). So top-1 at 2x and 3x act like top-8 near 1.1x and 1.6x. Above a top-subspace energy near that of the top-8 3x edit, the model degenerates into word strings that never reach an answer marker; every target edit stays below that level.

holds_against.why: Top-1 at 1x had 181 right against 170 for top-8 at 0.5x. Its cap hits match the energy law (51 vs 50), and an 11-problem difference in right answers is within the seed spread of one sample (up to 9).

mechanisms.statement: As an answer grows past 12,000 tokens, the terminator the model writes is less often attached to a derived result. Base and RL end long unsolved attempts by asserting a number (66-73 % of long wrong answers); Think-SFT keeps working but drifts into Chinese past about 13,600 tokens and rarely finishes right (1 of 24). So late tokens and late finishes pay little, except for undrifted Think-SFT traces, and RL-delta hosts convert late work at RL's low long-answer precision.

mechanisms.statement: In the terse register the base emits end-of-text almost right after its first stated result, with no check, so terse answers end within about 1,000 tokens and are wrong on any problem needing a longer derivation. A deliberative opening, self-opening, RL training or a later hold-on word lowers that post-result stop hazard. Scores of plain-prompt cells therefore depend on how many samples stay terse; on contest problems terse samples score almost nothing.
